questions.question: Man with kidney transplant had a recent small finger wound at a lake house. Worsening purulent SSTI despite multiple courses of antibiotics. Picture of hand with a purulent ulceration or two.Bacterial cultures negative, no acid-fast bacilli seen. There were a few white yeast-like colonies growing on Sabourad media, but they were thought to be contaminants and discarded. Shown below is the result of a periodic acid-Schiff stain of the lesion, demonstrating a morula-like “soccer ball” organism. (It’s protothecosis, apparently; I googled it after coming home. WTF.) [image-based question: periodic acid-Schiff stain image of the lesion showing a morula-like "soccer ball" organism was referenced but not included in this text export]

parts.text: What is the organism, to the genus level?
To what group does this organism belong?
What are two treatments for it?

questions.model_answer:
a) Organism (genus level): Prototheca.
b) Group: achlorophyllous (non-photosynthetic) algae.
c) Two treatments: (1) surgical debridement/excision of the lesion (2) systemic antifungal therapy, typically amphotericin B (itraconazole or voriconazole are alternative options), often combined with debridement and with reduction of immunosuppression.

parts.text: Name 2 diseases associated with algae blooms and for each one provide the associated toxin

questions.model_answer: (1) Ciguatera fish poisoning - ciguatoxin. (2) Paralytic shellfish poisoning - saxitoxin.

parts.text: List 2 non-infectious syndromes from toxigenic algae and their toxins

questions.model_answer: (1) Neurotoxic shellfish poisoning - brevetoxin. (2) Amnesic shellfish poisoning - domoic acid.

questions.question: A patient had a liver transplant 8 months ago. She has an injury to her R arm while at a cottage. Now has an ulcer with no lymphangitis. On staining from a sample, there are 'soccer ball' like morulas. The isolate grows on SAB within 7 days and colonies look like yeast morphologically, but the tech throws it out before working up. Blood and wound culture negative. No AFB.

cohort_answer.text: a) Prototheca. b) Chlorellaceae. c) Surgical debridement; Ampho B + tetracycline OR oral azole (e.g. itraconazole).

questions.question: Q54 2023 Day 2. List 2 non-infectious syndromes from toxigenic algae and their toxins. (PARASITIC)

parts.text: List 2 non-infectious syndromes from toxigenic algae and their toxins

cohort_answer.text: Ciguatera Fish Poisoning: toxin Ciguatoxin, formed by dinoflagellates of the genus Gambierdiscus (single-cell algae growing on coral reefs). Paralytic Shellfish Poisoning: toxin Saxitoxin, caused by ingestion of bivalve mollusks (mussels, clams, scallops, oysters) and crabs/snails contaminated with dinoflagellates of the genus Alexandrium (associated with red tides); symptoms within hours - perioral tingling, ataxia, difficulty swallowing, dizziness, paresthesias, weakness, paralysis, brainstem dysfunction, respiratory failure. Neurotoxic Shellfish Poisoning: ingestion of shellfish contaminated by Karenia brevis (formerly Gymnodinium breve, associated with red tides); GI distress and neurologic symptoms (paresthesias of face/mouth/extremities, dizziness, ataxia, muscle aches, temperature-related dysesthesia, seizures); symptoms typically resolve within 3 days.
